subject.title: feat(plugins): support per-agent plugin installation with --agent flag

question: Should OpenClaw accept a core `plugins install --agent` lifecycle now, and if so must it include runtime discovery, update, uninstall, doctor, docs, and security semantics in the same PR?
rationale: This is a new public CLI and persisted plugin lifecycle surface that affects plugin code execution, agent isolation, upgrades, and cleanup; automation cannot choose the durable product/security contract safely.

options.title: Pause for lifecycle contract
options.body: Require maintainer approval of the full per-agent plugin contract before repairing or merging this branch.

options.title: Narrow to an experimental design PR
options.body: Ask the contributor to split implementation away from the current branch and first document the intended install/discovery/update/uninstall semantics.

options.title: Proceed with end-to-end repair
options.body: Allow the PR to continue only if it repairs runtime scoping, update/uninstall behavior, validation, docs, and proof in one coherent change.

recommendation.title: Pause for lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Require maintainer approval of the full per-agent plugin contract before repairing or merging this branch.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the broadest plugin install, loader, and control-plane history and is the best available owner for the product boundary decision.
